source_gaps: The Apple iPhone password page has no Password AutoFill section, so AutoFill is not used. The Chrome steps are from the Show, edit, delete, or export section; the Edit and Delete wording is paraphrased. Nothing in these sources says that changing a password in the Passwords app also changes it with the website or app.

source_refs.title: Find saved passwords and passkeys on your iPhone - Apple Support
source_refs.section: View saved passwords and passkeys in Passwords
source_refs.applicability: iPhone with iOS 18 (the page says to use the Passwords app, update to iOS 18)
source_refs.verified_excerpt: To use the Passwords app, update to iOS 18.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone with iOS 18: Open the Passwords app. Unlock with Face ID or Touch ID, or enter your passcode. Choose a category or Shared Group, then select a website or app. To update a password, tap Edit, then tap Change Password. To delete a password or passkey, tap Edit, then tap Delete.

source_refs.title: Find saved passwords and passkeys on your iPhone - Apple Support
source_refs.section: View saved passwords and passkeys in iOS 17 or earlier
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Tap Settings, then scroll down and tap Passwords.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone with iOS 17 or earlier: Tap Settings, then scroll down and tap Passwords. Use Face ID or Touch ID when prompted, or enter your passcode. To view a password or passkey, select a website or app. To update a password, tap Edit. To delete a password or passkey, tap Delete Password or Delete Passkey.

source_refs.title: Manage passwords in Chrome - Computer - Google Chrome Help
source_refs.section: Show, edit, delete, or export saved passwords
source_refs.verified_excerpt: At the top right, select More and then Passwords and autofill and then Google Password Manager.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Chrome on a computer: At the top right, select More and then Passwords and autofill and then Google Password Manager. Under Passwords, select the password. On the right of your password, select Show password. To change it, select Edit, make your changes, then select Save. To remove it, select Delete.

source_refs.verified_excerpt: You can turn this option off or on at any time.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Chrome on a computer: Chrome offers to save passwords by default. To turn this off or on, go to Google Password Manager, select Settings, and change Offer to save passwords and passkeys. You can turn this option off or on at any time.
